page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 224 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes L1d cache of 32 KB, L2 cache of 0.5 MB, and L3 cache of 32 MB. No local NVMe storage or GPUs are bundled with this configuration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in PassMark memory testing and strong results in stress-ng multi-core CPU execution and PassMark CPU scores. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, resulting in strong PassMark CPU encryption performance. In application-specific benchmarks, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and single-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and gzip compression, fall within the average tier.

The c2d-standard-56 offers a resource-dense profile for multi-threaded workloads without the added cost of specialized GPU hardware. The absence of local SSD storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. Given its strong multi-core efficiency, database operations, and software compilation performance, this instance is suited for multi-threaded backend applications, compilation pipelines, database hosting, and medium-scale LLM text generation tasks.
